correction.text: "Gobero is located in the Ténéré desert of Niger" (coordinates 17 5 N 9 31 E; infobox "Location: Agadez, Niger"); Lake Gobero "around 3 km in diameter"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "Phase III dates from 5200 BCE to 2200 BCE"; a 100 km disc (117 land cells, about 30,000 km2) round the Gobero coordinates in the Ténéré desert stands for the Tenerian: the page gives the site (a lake 3 km across) and 182 burial sites, no area. The Kiffian (7700-6200 BCE) and the "interruption in the occupation of the site from 6200-5200 BCE" are not drawn.

region.text: "Gobero is located in the Ténéré desert of Niger" (coordinates 17 5 N 9 31 E; infobox "Location: Agadez, Niger"); Lake Gobero "around 3 km in diameter"

ledger.note: 5200 BCE: the Tenerian herders and fishers settle Lake Gobero in the Ténéré, Niger. "Phase III dates from 5200 BCE to 2200 BCE"; "who settled the area 1,000 or more years after the Kiffians"; the Kiffian site was interrupted "from 6200-5200 BCE". The year is the page's; the disc is the dossier's.

region.text: "Gobero is located in the Ténéré desert of Niger" (coordinates 17 5 N 9 31 E; infobox "Location: Agadez, Niger"); Lake Gobero "around 3 km in diameter"

ledger.note: 2200 BCE: the Tenerian occupation of Gobero ends as the Sahara dries. "Phase III dates from 5200 BCE to 2200 BCE"; "Phase IV, which dates from 2500 BCE to 300 BCE" is "the Sahara dries out once more, ending any occupation". The page contradicts itself on the end: infobox "Abandoned: c. 3000 BCE", "6250 BCE to 2550 BCE" in the Middle Holocene section.

certainty.note: A lake-side occupation; no border is recorded.

sources.title: Gobero
sources.note: Kiffian 7700-6200 BCE, interruption 6200-5200 BCE, Tenerian 5200-2200 BCE; Ténéré desert, Niger; coordinates 17.083 N 9.517 E; infobox abandoned c. 3000 BCE.

notes: Tenerian culture at Gobero, Niger. The Kiffian (page: Phase II 7700-6200 BCE, "probably remained in the region until around 6000 BCE") ends at or before the project floor and has no dossier. The page gives three Tenerian ends (2200, 2550, infobox 3000); 2200, the Phase III end, is used. Gobero and Ténéré are not in the gazetteer; a coordinate disc is used. Other Saharan cattle herders (Libya, Mauritania) are in saharan-neolithic-pastoralists and tichitt-tradition.
